project_title: RescuePulse — Disaster Intelligence & Rescue Prioritization Engine
project_description: RescuePulse turns the chaotic flood of unstructured disaster reports (SMS messages, social media posts, radio transcripts) into a prioritized, actionable rescue plan. During a disaster, emergency command centers are overwhelmed by thousands of fragmented messages — "300 people trapped on rooftops", "bridge washed out", "unconfirmed gas leak" — and manually triaging them costs hours that victims do not have. RescuePulse parses each report into a structured event (category, location, people affected, injured, dead, trapped), scores severity across six explainable dimensions (threat to life 34%, scale 20%, inherent hazard 18%, urgency with 2-hour half-life decay 14%, secondary risk 9%, source credibility 5%), ranks every report from CRITICAL to LOW, and attaches concrete resource bundles (medical teams, rescue teams, helicopters, boats, life jackets) to each priority. It runs fully offline in a single zero-dependency 40KB JavaScript file — deployable on a laptop in a disconnected disaster zone where cloud APIs fail — and is deterministic, so the same input always yields the same plan, enabling drills, audits, and trust. It accepts a single report, a batch file, or a stdin pipe, and exports both plain-text action plans and styled HTML reports for command-center screens.

commands: node tool.js --report "Landslide near Green Valley, 25 people stranded, 6 injured"
echo "Fire in warehouse district, 15 workers trapped" | node tool.js --reports -
code.self_test: 19/19 assertions passed (parsing, count extraction, severity monotonicity, urgency decay, deterministic ranking, HTML well-formedness, no forbidden markers, size limit)
algorithms: keyword-weighted multi-class event detection with event-type priority tiers
regex-based entity extraction (people, injured, dead, missing, trapped, location)
six-dimension weighted severity scoring with piecewise-log curves and exponential time decay
rule-based resource allocation per severity level and disaster category
FNV-1a hashing for deterministic report IDs
code.demo_url_suggestion: Host rescue-plan.html (generated via --demo --html) on any static host for the demo_url field.
